# Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture

This file is a Wikipedia-facing entry point for the formalization in
`FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«20»`.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower_(mathematics))
-/

@[expose] public section

reformulations.difference: This declaration is imported, not declared in the reviewed file. It uses exactly n-uniform families, the least threshold for cardinality ≥ m, and a strict exponential bound with natural-number bases. Wikipedia uses sets of size at most n, the threshold for cardinality > m, and a non-strict exponential bound for petal counts greater than two.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For positive n, padding each member with its own fresh elements makes a family n-uniform while preserving intersections between distinct members. Thus the uniform and bounded-size versions have the same thresholds. For positive petal counts the imported threshold is Wikipedia's threshold plus one, as Wikipedia explicitly explains using its alternative Sun notation. Increasing the exponential base to an integer greater than C+1 absorbs this additive one and changes ≤ to < for every n≥1; the reverse implication is immediate. Infinite families reduce to sufficiently large finite subfamilies. Petal counts 0, 1, and 2 have thresholds 0, 1, and 2 for positive n, so their inclusion adds no difficulty. Wikipedia's n=0 case is automatic. Hence the imported theorem poses the same conjecture.

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower_(mathematics) — definitions, threshold conventions, sunflower lemma, Erdős–Rado conjecture, and distinction from the solved weak conjecture.
Alweiss, Lovett, Wu, and Zhang, Improved bounds for the sunflower lemma, arXiv:1908.08483, §1 (LaTeX source read at https://arxiv.org/e-print/1908.08483).

review.notes: The reviewed 30-line file is solely a Wikipedia-facing entry point: it publicly imports FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«20» and contains no mathematical declarations or status metadata of its own. No file-level mismatch was found. The reformulation above records the imported conjecture's conventions for context. Scratch Lean checks successfully loaded the entry point, inspected the definitions, and proved boundary facts about empty/singleton sunflowers, the zero-petal threshold, and finiteness forced by positive ncard. Wikipedia continues to record the Erdős–Rado conjecture as open. Requests to erdosproblems.com/20 returned a JavaScript challenge; the comparison was established from the accessible cited Wikipedia page and the primary paper instead.
